w: Claims the title of the world's oldest picture garden still screening films today. Deckchairs face the screen under the open Kimberley sky, and unlike almost every other outdoor cinema on earth -- most run just one or two nights a week -- this one shows films most nights of the year.
s: World's oldest running outdoor picture garden
_facts: World's oldest picture garden still in operation
Screens multiple films most nights, unlike most outdoor cinemas which run 1-2 nights a week

w: Built in 1879 as a telegraph cable station linking Java to Australia, complete with a tennis court, billiard room and servants for the British staff. It operated until 1914 and gave Cable Beach its name -- the spot where the undersea cable came ashore. Now used as Broome's Court House.
_facts: Built 1879 as a cable station linking Java to Australia
Operated until March 1914; had a tennis court and billiard room for British staff
Cable Beach is named for the cable that came ashore here
Now used as Broome Court House; listed on the WA State Heritage Register

n: Anglican Church of the Annunciation, Broome
w: Known as the Little White Church, this wood-and-corrugated-iron chapel opened in 1903 as the Pro Cathedral of the Annunciation and has been in continuous use ever since -- one of Broome's oldest surviving places of worship.
_facts: Also called the Pro-Cathedral of the Annunciation and 'The Little White Church'
Continually used as a church since opening
